A partir de ese diagnóstico, redefine la agencia digital transformadora como un logro situado y colectivo, la articula con la soberanía digital y presenta el ciclo de reapropiación escolar de las decisiones digitales (CREDD), un modelo de acción en cinco fases. El artículo sostiene que potenciar la agencia exige intervenir a la vez sobre los repertorios de los actores y sobre las condiciones institucionales que delimitan sus posibilidades.

articles_hidden.title: Researcher well-being as a leading indicator in research-funding governance: A system dynamics exploration of top-down versus bottom-up allocation
articles_hidden.authors: Tomoko Sakai; Satoshi Sano
articles_hidden.abstract: Governments face a recurring dilemma in dividing public research funding between top-down, competitive, mission-oriented programmes and bottom-up, investigator-led institutional grants. This research note presents an exploratory system dynamics model that endogenizes researcher motivation, conceived following self-determination theory as a slow-moving stock of psychological capital, within the feedback structure linking funding allocation, research outputs, and societal returns. Simulation experiments across three policy scenarios reveal a consistent time-asymmetric pattern. First, accelerating the shift toward competitive funding produces an earlier but lower peak in societal returns, followed by sustained decline. Second, shifting toward bottom-up funding restores motivation but opens a transition valley in returns whose depth grows with transition speed. Third, delayed corrective reallocation exhibits hysteresis: once motivation is depleted, even aggressive reallocation requires roughly two decades before returns recover. One-at-a-time sensitivity analysis indicates that these qualitative patterns persist across the tested parameter ranges, while the level of long-run returns proves highly sensitive to the weight placed on discretionary research time, around which the baseline system undergoes a regime shift. The model implies that researcher well-being functions as a leading indicator of research-system health, preceding declines in publication-based lagging indicators. We derive three testable propositions and outline an agenda for empirical calibration, beginning with a national baseline survey of researchers being launched in Japan. For funding governance, the results imply that monitoring leading indicators and pacing allocation transitions matter as much as choosing the allocation ratio itself.

articles_hidden.title: Lexical, Syntactic, and Semantic Distances Across Five Languages: A Reproducible Framework Integrating Python NLP and R Statistical Modeling
articles_hidden.authors: Shunxin Yao
articles_hidden.abstract: Quantitative comparisons across languages have traditionally relied on manually curated typological features, while recent advances in multilingual language models provide new opportunities for large-scale cross-linguistic research. This paper presents a reproducible framework that integrates natural language processing and statistical modeling to examine lexical, syntactic, and semantic variation across English, Chinese, Spanish, French, and German. Drawing on a corpus of 1,860 Wikipedia articles, the study combines traditional linguistic indicators with LaBSE-based semantic representations. The results show that language differences dominate the observed variation, with Chinese forming a distinct outlier and English and Spanish exhibiting the greatest similarity. Moreover, lexical-syntactic distances are significantly correlated with semantic distances derived from Transformer embeddings. These findings suggest that traditional quantitative measures and modern representation-learning approaches capture complementary aspects of language structure and meaning. The framework offers a scalable methodology for multilingual corpus linguistics and quantitative typology.

articles_hidden.title: Position: A Score Should Travel With Its Repair History
articles_hidden.authors: Louis Yiven Zhu
articles_hidden.abstract: Machine learning settles many capability claims with scores on accepted benchmarks, and a venue reviews a benchmark once, when it accepts the paper that introduces it. We call this arrangement review once, use forever. We argue that it leaves without stewardship the instruments that, on the literature's account, carry much of the field's adjudication. Reforms of peer review in AI research should therefore extend to them. In the public record of MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding), five projects sharing no author with one another or with the original repaired four defects in 2024. Language model agents coded 194 passages in 26 documents under written rules. In the 170 reporting events, the passages that report a model's score, we test whether six qualifications accompany the score. Model reports attach 1.05 of six qualifications per event (95% interval [0.85, 1.32]) against 1.70 in the repair papers ([1.47, 2.08]). Of their 77 events, 21% carry no qualification ([10%, 31%]) and none carries an item-error qualification. After MMLU-Pro and MMLU-Redux appeared in June 2024, 19 of 28 model-report events on the original MMLU print a repaired variant beside it without its reason. On a second benchmark, Humanity's Last Exam, none of 14 events in nine 2026 model releases carries an item-error qualification. We propose three norms, with the cost of each to the actor who enforces it, and answer six alternative views.

articles_hidden.title: Single Family Schoolyards: Residential Zoning and School Segregation
articles_hidden.authors: Stan Nguyen Oklobdzija; Nicholas Marantz; Carolina Reid
articles_hidden.abstract: Though the Supreme Court's 1954 decision in Brown v. Board of Education outlawed explicit segregation of public schools, segregation has remained stubbornly persistent in the intervening decades. What explains continuous racial segregation in the absence of explicit policy? One possible driver is America's built environment designed with similar segregationist impulses but not subject to the same corrective legal action. Zoning and land use policy influence where households of different means can live, thereby sorting their children across schools. We investigate this link drawing on housing unit counts from the American Community Survey, apportioned to 923 school district boundaries and 13,002 school attendance zones with 27 million residential parcels. We find that districts where single-family and multifamily housing is spread unevenly across attendance zones are more segregated by race and income. Schools with attendance zones that contain a higher proportion of single-family detached residences enroll a disproportionately high share of Asian and White students, as compared with their districts. When an attendance zone boundary is redrawn to encompass a higher share of single-family housing, its Asian and White share increases further. These findings help illuminate how land use policy influences educational segregation and contributes to literature on how policies that regulate the built environment affect racial sorting.

articles_hidden.title: Machine-Learning Geographic Sampling Frames Underrepresent People on the Move in Fragile Settings
articles_hidden.authors: Andrea Carlomaria Caflisch; Daniel Masterson; Stephen Daniel O'Connell; Ettan Patel; Julia Smith Omomo
articles_hidden.abstract:
Political science research often studies difficult-to-locate populations: internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, migrants, and others who move during war, disaster,
or crisis. We compare machine-learning (ML)-generated building footprints against high-resolution satellite imagery for constructing sampling frames. In displacement-
affected communities in Iraq, 15.5% of ML points were invalid or duplicated, and manual additions constituted 19% of the final hybrid frame. Manual additions reached
10.2 percentage points more IDPs in rural communities and 10.1 more returnees in urban areas. We attribute differences to two mechanisms: temporary and informal
shelters are harder for ML algorithms to detect, while post-bombardment reconstruction can create structures absent from the imagery underlying ML frames. ML-only
frames produce systematic coverage error, and targeted satellite validation can reduce it.

articles_hidden.title: MAGA Republicans as  “Particularistic Authoritarians” on the Welfare State:  Parallels with the European Populist Right
articles_hidden.authors: Jake Haselswerdt; Hang Qi; Suhyun Cho
articles_hidden.abstract: Has MAGA remade the Republican politics of the welfare state? While Republican voters have traditionally favored retrenchment, the so-called “populism” of the MAGA movement suggests that the social policy preferences of right-leaning Americans are due for reexamination. Drawing from the “particularistic authoritarian model” of European populist radical-right voters, we expect MAGA Republicans to favor benefits for deserving groups, stronger “workfare” policies, less social investment, and more restrictive deservingness criteria. We test these expectations using a 1,000-respondent module of the 2025 Cooperative Election Study. Factor analysis and regressions show that MAGA Republicans are substantially more supportive than non-MAGA Republicans of policies benefiting seniors and express levels of support comparable to those of Democrats and other respondents. MAGA Republicans also show somewhat stronger endorsement of restrictive deservingness criteria than other Republicans, while differences between the two Republican groups are less pronounced for social investment. Overall, the results indicate that MAGA Republicans do not simply favor either welfare state expansion or retrenchment. Instead, they distinguish among forms of social protection according to their beneficiaries and perceived deservingness.

articles_hidden.title: Are the children of homeowners increasingly advantaged? Trends in relative and absolute mobility of homeownership in Europe
articles_hidden.authors: Selçuk Bedük; Enrico Benassi; Philipp M. Lersch
articles_hidden.abstract: Homeownership is declining among younger generations across Europe. A common assumption is that this decline has been increasingly stratified by parental homeownership, due to rising house prices and the growing importance of parental financial support. We show that this assumption does not hold for the average European (and for most countries). Using data from EU-SILC 2011 and 2019 covering 24 European countries, we examine trends in relative and absolute mobility of homeownership for birth cohorts 1951 to 1984. On average, relative mobility remained largely stable across cohorts, while absolute mobility increased. The apparent stability of relative mobility masks a deeper structural cohort shift: downward mobility increased from 14 per cent to 38 per cent, while upward mobility declined from 23 per cent to 8 per cent between cohorts born in the early 1950s and early 1980s. Therefore, homeownership has declined significantly for both children of homeowners and renters. We also compare absolute and relative mobility trends across countries and show that they often diverge for two reasons. First, a mechanical effect of the origin distribution: in countries with widespread parental homeownership, relative mobility largely reflects changes in upward mobility. Second, the source of mobility: using two novel counterfactual simulations, we show that observed absolute mobility changes mainly stem from structural shifts in homeownership chances, rather than strengthening parent-child associations.

articles_hidden.title: The Space Headright System: A Diachronic Analysis of First-Mover Elite Formation Mechanisms from Colonial Virginia to Twenty-First-Century Space Resource Law
articles_hidden.authors: Shungo Arai
articles_hidden.abstract:
This study examines how first-mover advantage was converted into durable elite dominance in seventeenth-century colonial Virginia, using this structural logic to critically evaluate twenty-first-century space resource law. Drawing on a Multilayered Frontier Capital Accumulation Model (MFCAM) that integrates frontier theory, world-systems theory, and institutional path dependence, the study addresses four research questions (RQ1–RQ4). Historical analysis shows how the First Families of Virginia (FFV), preempting land under the 1618 headright system, monopolized power through mutually reinforcing mechanisms of institutional pre-emption, marital closure, and symbolic capital accumulation, thereby converting land capital into political and cultural capital to maintain that dominance. At the same time, the study traces the formation of a lower-white stratum through indentured servitude, post-release landlessness, and racial divide-and-rule policies after Bacon's Rebellion (1676) and shows that elite and lower-class formation were two sides of the same institutional design. A comparison with the Massachusetts Bay Colony suggests these outcomes depended on early institutional choices.

Based on these findings, the study conceptualizes a "Space Headright System" (SHS) comprising priority access to institutional design, revolving-door relations between regulators and industry, and the accumulation of legal precedent. By examining Section 402 of the 2015 U.S. Commercial Space Launch Competitiveness Act, the Artemis Accords, and national space resource laws, it assesses risks of lower-class formation such as space indentured servitude and space company towns. The study advances a conditional warning: if current legal trajectories continue, they suggest convergence toward a Virginia-type stratified order. To avert this, three policy recommendations (primary rules)—an international space cadastre, a Space Commons Fund, and treaty-based protections for later settlers—are proposed, alongside secondary design requirements to guard the implementing institutions against regulatory capture.

articles_hidden.title: The Relationship between China's One-Child Policy and Female Empowerment
articles_hidden.authors: Wendi Wang; Qing Guan; Natalie Nitsche
articles_hidden.abstract: Vanessa Fong (2002) theorised that China's One-Child Policy (OCP; 1979–2016) enhanced female empowerment by removing competition from sons and allowing daughters to obtain resources traditionally reserved for sons. However, no systematic review has comprehensively assessed the available evidence on this issue. Drawing on Fong’s framework, we examined the relationship between the OCP and female empowerment across seven subfields: family investment and parental support, education, employment and career development, gender attitudes and norms, intergenerational relationships, reproductive rights and autonomy, and other social dynamics. We searched six scientific databases, yielding 1265 sources and, after applying exclusion criteria, analyzed 32 studies published between 2002 and 2024. The majority (21 of 32) report a positive relationship between the OCP and female empowerment. Resource concentration driven by reduced sibling size emerges as a central mechanism, benefiting only-daughters in family investment, education, and career development. In contrast, impacts on mothers are more mixed; while the OCP reduced childbirth burdens and enhanced life autonomy, it also violated reproductive rights and imposed disproportionate contraceptive burdens on women. Moreover, it emerges the OCP's empowering effects were contingent on external conditions, such as local educational and economic resources or place of residence. We point out various research gaps in the existing literature, amongst other the consistent failure to distinguish the OCP’s effects from concurrent socio-economic transformations. Nonetheless, the evidence suggests that the OCP, together with broader social changes, has shaped women's lives and promoted female empowerment, although its impacts were neither uniform nor inherent, but rather shaped by contextual factors.

articles_hidden.title: Measuring Students’ Attention Boundaries in GAI-Assisted Learning: Development and Validation of the GAI-Mediated Learning Boundary Scale and Latent Profile Analysis
articles_hidden.authors: XI ZHAN; Yuxiang Shi; Peiyun He
articles_hidden.abstract: The Generative AI (GAI) is reshaping the temporal and spatial organization of college learning and the perceived boundary crossing between teacher-assigned tasks and self-directed learning. This study developed and validated a scale to assess college students’ attention boundary management in GAI-mediated learning. Analyzing data from 1904 students at 3 colleges in China, the study established a five-dimensional structure: Flexibility, Fragmentation, Immersion, Positive Spillover, and Negative Spillover. Exploratory and Confirmatory Factor Analysis confirmed the scale’s psychometric properties. A Latent Profile Analysis identified four distinct student profiles, Protective, Strained, Overextended, and Engaged Permeability Management. Supplementary heterogeneity analyses examined differences across the four profiles by gender, grade level, university, purposes and duration of AI use, and other learning-related characteristics. Based on these, this study proposed profile-specific recommendations. The study provides a validated instrument for assessing students’ attention boundaries in GAI-mediated learning, identifies heterogeneous student profiles, and offers differentiated practical implications.

articles_hidden.title: Recordable participation and the construction of student engagement in UK higher education
articles_hidden.authors: Xinqi Yu
articles_hidden.abstract: Student engagement is widely invoked as evidence of educational quality, yet its meanings are contested. This article examines how the concept is constructed and mobilised in UK higher education research, policy and institutional documentation. Drawing on Bacchi’s problematisation approach and Fairclough’s critical discourse analysis, it analyses a purposive corpus of 36 texts: 23 conceptual and research texts, two policy documents and 11 institutional documents from three West Midlands universities. Iterative close reading identifies three connected patterns. Multidimensional accounts of engagement are narrowed into visible proxies; evaluative infrastructures privilege meanings that can be documented and compared; and these constructions redistribute responsibility in ways that obscure unequal conditions of participation. Worked coding examples show how support, attendance, digital traces and regular logging become linked in institutional procedures. The article argues that recordable participation acquires authority because it can serve as evidence of both student conduct and institutional quality. This does not eliminate relational or participatory meanings, but places them at a disadvantage within systems organised around demonstrable performance. The contribution is to explain how the demand for evidence connects conceptual narrowing to unequal recognition, and why institutions should distinguish the visibility of participation from the conditions that make participation possible.

articles_hidden.title: Resilience by Design: Adhocracy, Collaborative Governance, and Public-Private-Nonprofit Partnerships in Bergamo’s COVID-19 Economic Recovery
articles_hidden.authors: Paolo Valter Caroli; Francesco Longo
articles_hidden.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic revealed the vulnerabilities of traditional bureaucratic governance structures in responding effectively to rapid, large-scale crises. This paper presents a detailed case study of Rinascimento, an innovative urban recovery program launched in Bergamo, Italy—one of the epicenters of the early pandemic. It explores how an adhocratic governance model, characterized by :lexibility, decentralization, and cross-sector collaboration, was employed to mitigate the economic impact of the crisis. The program was implemented through a public-private-nonpro:it partnership involving the Municipality of Bergamo, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, and CESVI, a local humanitarian NGO. Drawing on collaborative governance and network theories, the Rinascimento initiative combined emergency grants and impact investment loans to support nearly 4,500 small businesses and professionals. The paper analyzes the design and operational mechanisms of the adhocracy, its rapid decision-making capabilities, and its emphasis on real-time learning and adaptation. Empirical evaluation using key performance indicators demonstrates the program’s effectiveness in enhancing business resilience, reducing business mortality rates, and fostering economic regeneration. The :indings underscore the potential of adhocratic models in municipal crisis management and offer scalable insights for future governance frameworks addressing systemic shocks.

articles_hidden.title: From Governance to Government? The European Commission and the three faces of politicisation
articles_hidden.authors: Francesco Nicoli; Lorenzo Lombardi
articles_hidden.abstract: Research on the politicisation of the European Union has concentrated on reactive, bottom-up contestation of existing EU action. This article argues that such an understanding is incomplete because it conflates politicisation of issues with politicisation of institutions. We distinguish three faces of politicisation. Reactive politicisation refers to the public contestation of existing EU competences. Proactive politicisation occurs when supranational actors claim a political mandate in order to justify wider discretion. Induced politicisation emerges when intergovernmental conflict over already politicized state functions creates a vacuum that the Commission can try to fill, thereby inheriting the political character of the function itself. The empirical sections focus on induced politicisation. They reconstruct three episodes: Jean-Claude Juncker's attempt to use EMU deadlock to place the Commission at the centre of euro-area reform; the failed institutionalisation of an EU Finance Minister, a euro-area fiscal capacity, and a more political treasury function; and Ursula von der Leyen's attempts to centralise foreign-policy initiative during successive geopolitical crises. The argument is that politicisation does not only constrain supranational action. Under specific institutional conditions it can also widen supranational authority by transforming the Commission from guardian of the Treaties into a proto-governmental executive.

articles_hidden.title: Sectoral Credit Reallocation and Consumer Credit Expansion: A Difference-in-Differences and Decomposition Analysis
articles_hidden.authors: Gudzenko Vladislav
articles_hidden.abstract: This article examines sectoral bank-credit reallocation in Kyrgyzstan by combining a difference in differences (DiD) comparison around 2015 with a detailed accounting analysis for 2019–2025. The research question is how conclusions about reallocation depend on the comparison period, portfolio denominator and distinction between shares and real balances. Four focal lending categories are compared with a residual category in a historical series extended through 2025. The full-portfolio DiD contrast is +1.28 percentage points for 2010–2025, but −0.17 points when the window begins in 2012; the group gap already changes substantially before 2015. In the recent period, consumer loans rise from 11.8% to 33.6% of bank credit and account for 42.5% of the nominal increase in the outstanding portfolio. CPI-deflated non-consumer credit grows by 49.3%. Agriculture loses portfolio share while its real balance grows by 12.3%; industry and construction experience real declines of 34.7% and 17.5%. A symmetric decomposition separates the changing consumer-credit mix from redistribution within non-consumer lending. The integrated findings show why positive period-average sectoral contrasts can coexist with recent share losses and uneven real growth. DiD remains descriptive, and the decomposition is an accounting identity. Neither identifies the effect of accession or consumer-credit crowding out. Independent verification of the historical inputs remains incomplete.

articles_hidden.title: Analisis Value Chain Upgrading Komoditas Kakao melalui Strategi Branding dan Diferensiasi Produk di Sabang
articles_hidden.authors: Daudy Sukma; Sofia Keumalasari; Azlina; Zahriatul Aini; Aulia Hafizah Nazwa
articles_hidden.abstract:
Kakao Sabang memiliki potensi terroir — rasa dan aroma khas — namun
produksi dan luas lahan menurun dalam lima tahun terakhir, dengan mayoritas
biji masih dijual non-fermentasi bernilai rendah. Penelitian kualitatif ini
memetakan rantai nilai (value chain analysis atau VCA) dan mengidentifikasi peluang peningkatan nilai (value chain upgrading atau VCU) kakao Sabang
melalui wawancara mendalam terhadap petani, pengumpul, UMKM pengolah,
dan Dinas Pertanian Kota Sabang, dilengkapi triangulasi sumber. Hasil
menunjukkan premi harga fermentasi mencapai 200 persen, namun hanya
terealisasi pada jalur petani–UMKM, belum pada jalur pengumpul umum.
Ditemukan pola functional upgrading organik berupa UMKM yang berperan
sebagai pengumpul mutu. Penelitian ini merumuskan strategi branding berbasis
marketing mix 7-P dengan perspektif consumer agency, merekomendasikan
perluasan insentif fermentasi dan formalisasi Indikasi Geografis sebagai
instrumen branding jangka panjang.

articles_hidden.title: El Encuadre de la Responsabilidad Ciudadana: Comunicación Digital del Servel en la Elección Presidencial y Parlamentaria 2025
articles_hidden.authors: Jaime Elorrieta
articles_hidden.abstract:
Los organismos electorales enfrentan un desafío comunicacional distinto al de los partidos o candidaturas: deben informar y movilizar al electorado sin abandonar su mandato de neutralidad. Este informe examina cómo el Servicio Electoral de Chile (Servel) resolvió ese desafío en su publicidad digital durante la elección presidencial y parlamentaria de 2025, a partir del análisis de 101 anuncios publicados en Google Ads y Meta Ads.
Los resultados muestran que la comunicación del Servel es abrumadoramente práctica: el 85,1% de los anuncios se centra en información procedimental —dónde votar, qué documentos llevar, cómo revisar el rol de vocal de mesa— por sobre la apelación emocional, cívica o sancionatoria. Contra lo esperable, el tono no escala hacia la urgencia a medida que se acerca la elección; en cambio, mensajes puntuales como el llamado al deber cívico o la alerta contra la desinformación aparecen concentrados en momentos específi cos de la campaña, no en un crescendo progresivo. La advertencia sobre multas por no votar, pese a ser un rasgo central del sistema electoral chileno, ocupa un lugar marginal (3% de la muestra) en la comunicación digital del organismo.

articles_hidden.title: Insights into the scale, organisation, implementation and motivations behind dog culling in a rabies-endemic setting
articles_hidden.authors: tasmin alexander; Kennedy Lushasi; Lwitiko Sikana; Anna Czupryna; Elaine Ferguson; Mirava Yuson; Deborah Nadal; Nicholas Hanley; Nai Rui Chng; Sarah Cleaveland
articles_hidden.abstract: Culling is recognised as ineffective and potentially counterproductive for sustainable dog population management and rabies control, yet the practice persists in many countries. Empirical data on the scale, organisation, implementation and motivations behind culling remain sparse, limiting understanding of its persistence, and implications. Focusing on Tanzania, a rabies-endemic country where culling has been documented, this study uses a mixed-methods approach, combining two structured surveys (survey of occurrence, n = 51; survey of practice in districts reporting culling, n = 16) and in-depth interviews with district and field-based veterinary and livestock officers (n = 8). Culling was reported in 45% of surveyed districts (23/51). Culling events were reportedly led by veterinary departments, often with involvement of other sectors and communities, with officers also describing communities as carrying out some culling independently. Culling was motivated by complaints, requests and orders about the number of and harms attributed to free-roaming dogs. Roaming dogs were culled regardless of ownership, sterilisation and vaccination status, using methods inconsistent with humane killing standards. Extrapolating from the survey data, using a stochastic simulation, we estimate approximately 26,000 dogs (95% CI 20,000-33,000) are culled annually nationwide. Culling was difficult to reconcile with evidence-based international guidance on dog population management and rabies control, national animal welfare legislation, and One Health principles, underscoring the need to understand and address the factors sustaining it. Addressing culling will require engaging with the wider concerns motivating the practice, and with the sectors and communities involved.

articles_hidden.title: Accountability Among Allies: Intra-Party Competition and the Electoral Cost of Scandal
articles_hidden.authors: Stefano Sangiovanni; Giovanna Maria Invernizzi; Andrea Ceron
articles_hidden.abstract: When do voters electorally punish politicians for scandals? We argue that a scandal changes votes only when it can tip voters who are near indifference between candidates, and that intra-party contests place far more voters in that position than inter-party contests. We formalize this argument in a model of electoral sanctioning and test it in a pre-registered conjoint experiment on 3,000 U.S. adults. The scandal penalty is about 57% larger in intra-party contests, and, as the model predicts, the amplification appears even when both candidates come from the party the voter opposes. Inter-party choice settings may therefore understate how strongly voters punish misconduct when credible co-partisan alternatives are available.

articles_hidden.title: Self-Employment in Mothers’ Careers After First Birth: A Comparison of South Korea and the United States
articles_hidden.authors: Wonjeong Jeong
articles_hidden.abstract: Upon parenthood, women face pressure to reorganize their paid work and careers. In this process, self-employment can offer a distinct option, with a different set of risks and benefits than wage work. Yet research on mothers’ employment trajectories rarely examines self-employment as a distinct option. This paper examines how self-employment fits into mothers’ careers after their first birth and how this pattern differs between two institutional contexts: South Korea and the United States. Using the Korean Labor and Income Panel Study and the Panel Study of Income Dynamics, I track mothers’ employment history from their first birth through the following ten years. Descriptive and sequence analyses show that one in five mothers experiences self-employment at least once, but the way they leverage it differs by institutional context. In South Korea, self-employment more often follows nonemployment, is primarily full-time, and occurs within trajectories leading back to paid work. In the United States, mothers more often enter self-employment from wage work, while part-time self-employment appears intermittently in wage-centered trajectories. Thus, self-employment occupies different positions across these two contexts, where mothers’ counterfactual career options vary. As technology shifts, the potential importance of diverse forms of self-employment, including contract-based gig work, may increase, raising the need for future research to examine how self-employment fits into one’s career.

articles_hidden.title: Data Report:   Anchoring International Law’s Dynamism (ANCHOR)  project
articles_hidden.authors: MOBILE - Center of Excellence for Global Mobility Law; Anouk Lamé; Sarah Scott Ford; Nora Stappert
articles_hidden.abstract:
How are interpretive shifts at international courts accepted or resisted within the day-to-day work of domestic legal systems? Over the past few years, several international courts have faced critique by policymakers for developing international law too dynamically. Consequently, scholarly literature has argued that we are entering a period of backlash, with states actively trying to hedge against the domestic impact of international rulings. Yet, little is known about how – and under what conditions – interpretive shifts are received within the day-to-day work of domestic legal systems, especially at lower and specialized courts. 

This data report describes the data used for the research conducted as part of the research project entitled “Anchoring International Law’s Dynamism: Tracing Denmark’s Reception of International Rulings” (ANCHOR). Focusing on international refugee and migration law as a critical test case, the project analyses case data from the Danish Refugee Appeals Board (RAB) to examine the domestic reception of international rulings. The data report begins by describing the data collection process across its different data sources, after which it turns to data processing. The report then outlines the extraction and qualitative coding of citations to international rulings, ending with a brief discussion of the choices made for the data analysis.

articles_hidden.title: “It’s Hard to See It Through Clinical Eyes When It’s Yourself”:    General Practice and Community Healthcare Professionals’ Experiences of Domestic Abuse, Disclosure, & Help-Seeking
articles_hidden.authors: Sandi Dheensa; Rebecca Cox; Judith Worthington; Paula Whittaker; Gene Feder; Alison Gregory
articles_hidden.abstract:
Background
Domestic abuse is highly prevalent and causes wide-ranging harms. Healthcare professionals are especially likely to receive disclosures and international policies call for a robust healthcare response to abuse.  But the needs of affected healthcare professionals (HCPs) have been sidelined. Globally, 42% of female HCPs report lifetime experience of domestic abuse. Our study aimed to explore how experiencing domestic abuse affects HCPs to understand the safety and support interventions needed. 
Methods
We used semi-structured interviews with 18 National Health Service primary and community HCPs and used Framework Analysis, drawing on four interrelated concepts: problem recognition, stigma, candidacy, and professional identity.  
Results
Perpetrators used HCP-survivors’ roles against them and domestic abuse had wide-ranging consequences for work. Remaining themes mapped onto HCP-survivors’ trajectory towards support, including problems with recognising and/or naming domestic abuse, the impact of recognising and naming it, reflections on different support options, consequences of workplace disclosure, support experiences, and reflections on what needs to change. Professional identity and profession-related factors affected each aspect of this trajectory, delaying recognition of domestic abuse and making help-seeking and positive support experiences less likely.  
Conclusion
Building an effective and compassionate healthcare response to domestic abuse will be impossible without attending to HCP-survivors’ needs and the inadequate responses of fellow HCPs. HCP-survivors are likely assets in improving responses to patients, colleagues, and students; but without support may experience trauma symptoms. We recommend improved first-line responses to HCP-survivors in workplaces and a move towards a recognition of HCPs as potential survivors in domestic abuse education, funding, and interventions.

articles_hidden.title: Closure without Resolution in European Prison Oversight
articles_hidden.authors: Nasrul Ismail
articles_hidden.abstract: Compliance with judgments of the European Court of Human Rights is conventionally recorded as a terminal status: a case is open or closed, a judgment executed or pending, an obligation met or unmet. These measures enable scholarly comparison, but they cannot show how a state engages with the supervision of a judgment or whether reform of prison conditions endures. As such, this article treats compliance as conduct and asks whether the closure of supervision reflects durable improvement in the conditions a judgment addressed. Drawing on the documentary record of Committee of Ministers supervision in three pilot-judgment jurisdictions (i.e., Italy, Romania, and Hungary), with two contextual comparators (i.e., Spain and England and Wales), it codes state disclosures for opacity and stance and reconstructs responsiveness descriptively from the dated supervisory sequence. Two independent coders reached strong agreement (Krippendorff’s alpha of 0.88 for stance and 0.90 for opacity, on small, well-specified eligible data sets). The cases did not form a single compliance scale but displayed distinct configurations. Specifically, Italy was transparent but shifted in its stated position before closure in 2016; Romania combined continuing engagement with capacity explanations; and Hungary combined formal but insubstantial engagement with selective disclosure. Set against current prison occupancy, the state that had completed supervision was the most overcrowded: Italy recorded 120.7 occupants per 100 places, exceeding Hungary's 114.5 and Romania's 111.2. Because the occupancy snapshot postdated Italy's closure, it could not reveal whether closure caused the later overcrowding, but it did manifest that closure did not secure lasting improvement in reforms. The article frames this durability gap as a problem of means-ends decoupling and offers a reproducible method for distinguishing compliance conduct from the substantive conditions oversight exists to change.

articles_hidden.title: Beyond Good and Bad Controls: Endogenous Legal Factors in Sentencing Research
articles_hidden.authors: Jose Pina-Sánchez; Andrzej Uhl
articles_hidden.abstract: Observational studies of institutional decision-making often rely on explanatory variables that are themselves partly constructed through the process under investigation. In sentencing research, many legal factors are defined by the judge and may therefore act simultaneously as confounders and mediators. Controlling for them may introduce post-treatment bias, whereas omitting them may reintroduce confounding bias. We propose overcoming this impasse by conceptualising judicially-defined legal factors as variables affected by measurement error. Using a typical regression model of racial disparities in the U.S. Federal Courts, we demonstrate how sensitivity analyses based on SIMEX and Monte Carlo simulations can be used to assess the bias arising from judicial disagreement and judicial prejudice. We show that even modest levels of uncertainty in discretionary legal factors can generate substantial and unpredictable bias, affecting estimates of racial disparities even when measurement error is entirely random and therefore unrelated to race.

articles_hidden.title: The Self-Destruction Hypothesis of Consumerism: The Inflation of Consumption Standards and the Mismatch with Household Income
articles_hidden.authors: ZY Liu; Di Yuan
articles_hidden.abstract: This paper proposes and develops a theoretical proposition concerning the endogenous evolution of consumerism: consumerism may not necessarily come to an end because of “excessive consumption”; rather, by continuously raising the consumption standards associated with “normal life,” it may make an increasing number of ordinary workers unable to participate in the consumption patterns it has itself constructed, thereby eroding the demand base on which it depends. Consumer demand has a positive expansionary effect during the early stages of economic development. The paper then explains why social consumption standards may continue to rise through three channels: firm competition; positional goods and social comparison; and the diffusion and amplification of cultural products and social media. On this basis, it argues that under conditions of market competition, firms simultaneously need to expand effective demand on the consumer side and have an inherent incentive to control labor costs, creating a structural mismatch between the growth of workers’ incomes and the rise of consumption standards. When consumption standards grow persistently faster than the actual disposable incomes of ordinary workers, consumption behavior may shift from “keeping up with the standard” toward “reducing, postponing, or even exiting consumption,” with particularly concentrated effects in marriage and family formation. Using the decline in China’s marriage and birth rates, the rising consumption standards associated with wedding photography and housing, and the adjustment of the real-estate sector as illustrative empirical cases, the paper distinguishes two post-turning-point adjustment paths—“structural consumption downgrading” and “aggregate-demand-driven consumption contraction”—and discusses the possibilities and limits of external trade as a substitute for domestic demand. The paper further constructs a conceptual income–consumption-standard mismatch model to characterize the pressure generated by the divergence between income and consumption standards and its transmission to consumption behavior, family formation, and future demand. Finally, it proposes four policy directions: optimizing social-media algorithms, establishing a Departmental Employment Quality Index (DEQI) for higher education, reducing the minimum cost of basic living, and limited government intervention in consumption externalities.
